oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Evolution of Empowerment: Black Women in Counselor Education Programs Before, During, and After the Pandemic
oai_dc:dc.dc:creator: Williams, Cynthia
LeAnn Morgan
oai_dc:dc.dc:subject: transcendental
counselor education
COVID-19
qualitative
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Black women in counselor education and supervision (CES) doctoral programs have historically been underrepresented in the scholarly literature, making it vital to understand how this group of women coped with the adverse effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. Employing Moustakas’s modified van Kaam’s systematic methods for conducting phenomenological research, we explored Black women’s lived experiences in CES doctoral programs prior to and amidst the pandemic. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with nine Black women enrolled in CES doctoral programs. Four main themes emerged: success factors, supportive networks and coping, academic, and personal challenges. The findings provide counselor educators and counseling professionals with information to consider utilizing culturally specific resources, increase an understanding of historical factors, and foster ways to build relationships with Black students.
